{"id":15,"answer":"From your notes (entry 12, your SQLite FTS5 note):

- bm25() ranking: lower is better — the score is negative-flavored, so a smaller value means a better match.
- Correct query pattern: ORDER BY rank, not by bm25 ascending. Ordering by bm25 directly gives you the worst matches first.
- External content tables (content= tables) don't update themselves: you need triggers to keep the FTS index in sync with the base table.

Source note: the three points above come entirely from your saved note. Nothing else in your notes covers FTS5 — the nearby entries are about systems thinking, retrieval architecture decisions (lexical + graph, embeddings deferred to v2), and unrelated study items, so I haven't pulled anything from them.

General knowledge (not from your notes), if useful: the usual trigger trio is AFTER INSERT, AFTER UPDATE, and AFTER DELETE on the base table, issuing INSERT/DELETE against the FTS table; the FTS5 'delete' command form is needed for external-content deletes because the index can't read the old column values from the content table at delete time.
